textbook: Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE GENERIC PLANT CELL — the classic whole-cell teaching diagram — centred in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with generous negative space around it so labels can attach later. A generous corner wedge of the cell is cut away so the interior shows in section. THE INTERIOR IS DOMINATED BY ONE ENORMOUS CENTRAL VACUOLE filling more than three quarters of the cell: a single compartment of pale, watery, translucent blue — optically clear sap, calm and empty — bounded by ONE thin deeper-blue membrane line (the tonoplast). (3) A FEW (two or three) clearly SMALLER bean-shaped MITOCHONDRIA tucked between the chloroplasts, each with a smooth steel-blue outer membrane and an inner membrane folding inward as wide wavy dusty-rose #C98A7A cristae ribbons like a rippled curtain — rose and wavy, entirely different from the green coin-stack chloroplasts. (4) ROUGH ER as short connected folded grey-blue #9AA7B5 cisternae flowing out of the nucleus's outer envelope line, stippled with tiny dark slate ribosome dots. (5) ONE small SEPARATE GOLGI stack of four or five smooth flattened dusty sage-green #8FAE8B cisternae with tiny vesicles at the rims. (6) A fine scatter of tiny dark slate ribosome dots and a few fine pale cytoskeleton threads along the strip. (7) A few PLASMODESMATA: thin cream cytoplasm threads crossing the full thickness of the sand-coloured wall band. Composition: the boxy cell fills most of the frame with quiet dark-charcoal space around it for labels; single specimen; refined, elegant, softly dimensional.
